utility.notes: Loudoun County is genuinely split between two electric providers — Dominion Energy Virginia serves most of Northern Virginia, while Northern Virginia Electric Cooperative (NOVEC), a member-owned cooperative, separately serves a substantial concentrated portion of the county (NOVEC alone reports roughly 33,000 Loudoun County customers, most within about 5 miles of its own Evergreen Mills Road facility) — this is not a clean geographic north/south split like some other multi-utility states researched this marathon, and this specific record does not independently verify which provider serves a majority of Loudoun's residential parcels. Dominion is recorded here as the more broadly-described provider per general reporting, with confidence lowered accordingly; a solar applicant in Loudoun County should confirm their own provider directly rather than assume.

value.name: Dominion Energy Virginia
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Loudoun County's residential solar customers this session; Dominion Energy Virginia is recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility for the portion of the county it serves — see the utility field notes on the genuine Dominion/NOVEC split within the county.

permit_authority.value: Loudoun County Department of Building and Development, Permitting Division
permit_authority.notes: Virginia's Uniform Statewide Building Code (USBC) is administered centrally by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) and its Board of Housing and Community Development, but enforcement — including permit fees, application processes, staffing, and review timelines — is delegated to each local government's own building department. Loudoun County's own Department of Building and Development is the permitting authority for unincorporated county areas; incorporated towns within the county (e.g., Leesburg, Purcellville) may operate their own separate building departments and would be separate AHJs not covered by this record.
